results.claim: The sky's blue color is not a reflection of the ocean.
Sunlight is composed of multiple wavelengths (white light) and collides with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere.
Blue light has shorter wavelengths and higher energy, causing it to scatter more than other colors (Rayleigh scattering).
Violet light has an even shorter wavelength than blue light.
Human eyes have receptors (cones) that are more sensitive to blue wavelengths than violet wavelengths.
Human perception registers the scattered blue light in the atmosphere, making the sky appear blue.
